docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This system uses a PIC18F47Q10 microcontroller and an ESP32 Wi-Fi module to control and monitor a motor over a wireless network. The PIC controls the motor driver to set the motor’s direction, turns an LED on or off to indicate the system is working, and reads a hall-effect sensor to measure the motor's rotation. The ESP32 communicates with the PIC and connects to an MQTT server over Wi-Fi, sending motor status and sensor data and receiving control commands from other devices. This setup allows the motor to be controlled remotely while providing feedback on its operation.

docs.title: Module's Selected Major Components
docs.text:
The following sections are the selected major components of the drive train for the scavenger tank.

Mircocontroller 1. ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N4

  • $5.06/each

  • link to product

    Pros Cons Inexpensive might have to create a circuit with it to make it easier to program Has many pins to use Limited Pins Has EDA/CAD file

Rationale: The ESP32 is a familiar component used in a previous class. The only issue is creating the PCB for all the components since I can't use the dev board with it. But it will be able to work with the other microcontrollers to send signals back and forth.

Motor Driver

  1. IC MTR DRV BIPLR 2.5-5.5V TSOT23

* $0.83/each
* [link to product](https://www.digikey.com/en/products/detail/monolithic-power-systems-inc/MP6513LGJ-Z/7361426)

| Pros                                      | Cons                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Inexpensive                               | Max Voltage supply is 5.5V                                       |
| Has thermal, current, and short circuit projection  | Low Max Current                                        |
| Has EDA/CAD file                          | More for smaller applications like cameras and toys              |
  1. IC BRUSHED MOTOR DRVR 8TSSOP

  • $0.83/each

  • link to product

    Pros Cons Inexpensive Only for DC brushed motors High Voltage & Current intake Sensitive thermal conditions Has EDA/CAD file Motor output current setting pin might be difficult to set up

  • IFX9201SGAUMA1

  • $3.55/each

  • link to product

    Pros Cons familiar component Only for DC brushed motors Protection Features 12V Has EDA/CAD file Motor output current setting pin might be difficult to set up

Rationale: IFX9201SGAUMA1 is a part we used in class. Already familiar with setting up and coding. Know it uses I^2C while the other components are unsure if they use I^2C.

DC Motors

  1. STANDARD MOTOR 6600 RPM 12V

  • $2.75/each
  • link to product

* | Pros | Cons | | ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | | cheap | Low torque, gear ratio may be needed | | can intake 12V | need custom footprint | | 2-wire setup | Little data on the datasheet |

  1. GEARMOTOR 35 RPM 12V MICRO METAL

  • $37.95

  • link to product

  • | Pros                                      | Cons                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| uses 12V                                  | High power                                                       |
| high torque                               | need custom footprint                                            |
| simple 2-wire connection                  | Might be too slow for the drive train                            |

  • GEARMOTOR 220 RPM 12V MICR METAL

  • $26.45

  • link to product

  • | Pros                                      | Cons                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| uses 12V                                  |  may not be enough torque or fast enough                         |
| steady speed                               | need custom footprint                                           |
| simple 2-wire connection                  | may not be suitable for a drive train                            |

Rationale: The GEARMOTOR 220 RPM 12V MICR METAL seems to be the best fit for the drive train system. Not only does it use 12V, but it has a balance of torque and speed that should be able to haul the weight of the rest of the scavenger tank.

Table 1: Example component selection

External Clock Module

Solution Pros Cons Option 1. XC1259TR-ND surface mount crystal$1/eachlink to product * Inexpensive[^1]* Compatible with PSoC* Meets surface mount constraint of project * Requires external components and support circuitry for interface* Needs special PCB layout. * Option 2. * CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator * $1/each * Link to product * Outputs a square wave * Stable over operating temperature * Direct interface with PSoC (no external circuitry required) range * More expensive * Slow shipping speed

Choice: Option 2: CTX936TR-ND surface mount oscillator

Rationale: A clock oscillator is easier to work with because it requires no external circuitry in order to interface with the PSoC. This is particularly important because we are not sure of the electrical characteristics of the PCB, which could affect the oscillation of a crystal. While the shipping speed is slow, according to the website if we order this week it will arrive within 3 weeks.

docs.title: Message Compliance Verification System
docs.text: Author: Tim Desanti Course: EGR 314 – Embedded Systems Design

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The Final Node is responsible for message validation and actuation within the system.

It ensures that only compliant messages: - Follow the required schema - Pass checksum validation - Contain valid command values

are allowed to control hardware outputs.

docs.title: 2. System Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Subscribe to incoming MQTT messages
  • Validate message structure
  • Verify checksum correctness
  • Execute motor control logic
  • Publish validation result

docs.title: 3.1 Pin Configuration
docs.text: Signal Pin Description SCK 10 SPI Clock MOSI 12 SPI Data Out MISO 8 SPI Data In CS 11 Chip Select DIS 9 Motor Enable PWM 18 Motor Speed DIR 16 Motor Direction BUTTON 13 User Input LED 4 Status Indicator

docs.title: 4.1 Protocol
docs.text: • MQTT over TCP/IP

docs.title: 4.2 Broker
docs.text: broker.hivemq.com

docs.title: 4.3 Topics
docs.text: Direction Topic Subscribe team301/final/input Publish team301/final/status

docs.title: 5.1 Input Message Format
docs.text:
{
  "node_id": "string",
  "timestamp": 12345,
  "payload": {
    "command": "ON" | "OFF"
  },
  "checksum": 123
}

docs.title: 6.1 Structural Requirements
docs.text: The message MUST include: - node_id - timestamp - payload.command - checksum

docs.title: 6.2 Data Constraints
docs.text: Field Requirement node_id Non-empty string timestamp Integer > 0 command "ON" or "OFF"

docs.title: 6.3 Checksum Definition
docs.text: checksum = (sum of ASCII values of command) % 256

docs.title: Example
docs.text: "ON" → 79 + 78 = 157 → checksum = 157

docs.title: 7. System Behavior
docs.text: Condition Motor LED Status Output VALID + ON ON ON VALID VALID + OFF OFF ON VALID INVALID OFF OFF INVALID

docs.title: 8. State Machine
docs.text: IDLE → RECEIVE → VALIDATE → ACT → REPORT → IDLE

docs.title: 9.1 Valid Message
docs.text: mosquitto_pub -h broker.hivemq.com -t team301/final/input -m '{"node_id":"node3","timestamp":12345,"payload":{"command":"ON"},"checksum":157}'

docs.title: 9.2 Expected Result
docs.text:
• Motor turns ON
  • LED turns ON
  • MQTT publishes: VALID

docs.title: 10. Compliance Summary
docs.text: This implementation provides: - Deterministic validation logic - Strict schema enforcement - Verified checksum computation - Observable system behavior
